# IEUM Concierge

> IEUM Concierge (이음, Korean for "a joining" or "connection") is a private luxury wellness travel concierge based between Seoul and New York. It plans, books, and runs fully bespoke journeys through Korea end to end, across Seoul, Jeju, Busan, Gyeongju, and the regions between, and also plans corporate events in Korea and advises Korean brands entering Europe and the United States.

Wellness sits at the centre of every journey IEUM designs. It is not one option among several. Korea's culture, beauty, and cuisine are woven through it, whatever shape the trip takes: a family holiday, a milestone celebration, or time alone. Because IEUM handles the researching, routing, planning, and booking, and stays reachable throughout, clients take a true vacation and come home rested, refreshed, and rejuvenated, with no need for a second holiday to recover from the first.

Founded by Doha Yoon. Every itinerary is designed individually and never sold as a package. IEUM works most often with travelers from Europe, the United States, and Latin America. Everything is delivered in English and Korean, with French and Spanish speaking guides arranged on request. Services include private drivers, personal translators, expert cultural guides, restaurant and experience reservations that are not available to book online, and 24 hour concierge support for the duration of a trip.

IEUM works across the whole of Korea, not only Seoul. Journeys run in Seoul, Jeju, Busan, Gyeongju, Sokcho, and the smaller places between them, in every season, for stays from a few days to a few weeks.

## Services

- [Private Journeys](https://ie-um.com/private-journeys.html): Fully bespoke luxury itineraries through Korea, planned, booked, and run end to end. Wellness is at the centre of every journey: temple stays in the mountains, hot spring towns, jjimjilbang bathhouse traditions, and the quieter regions where Koreans go to rest, from Seoraksan to Jeju. Woven through it are Korea's culture (hanbok at the palaces, artisan workshops, private museum visits), beauty (hanbang facials, dermatology clinics, Seoul styling studios), and cuisine (restaurants that do not take online reservations, royal cuisine cooking classes, market mornings). Journeys then take the shape of the occasion: Family Journeys built for travelling with children, including dietary needs, accessibility and split day planning; Milestone Journeys for proposals, anniversaries and birthdays; and Solo and Couple Journeys for restorative time away. Every journey includes itinerary design and booking, a private driver, personal translator, private cultural guide, and 24 hour concierge support.
- [Corporate Events](https://ie-um.com/corporate-events.html): Corporate retreats, incentive travel, and off-sites staged in Korea. Includes venue sourcing, negotiated group accommodation, transport, professional translation, on site coordination, and themed events.
- [Consulting](https://ie-um.com/consulting.html): Market entry consulting for Korean brands expanding into Europe and the United States. Covers branding and marketing strategy, go to market strategy and planning, and local operations and recruitment.

## Common questions answered on this site

- Do I need a visa to visit Korea? Most travellers, including citizens of the United States, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand, can currently enter Korea without a K-ETA through 31 December 2026 under a temporary exemption covering 67 countries. An e-Arrival card is still required within three days of arrival.
- How many days should I plan for a first visit to Korea? Ten days is a comfortable minimum to see Seoul, Busan, and Jeju without rushing, though shorter well designed itineraries work well with a concierge handling logistics.
- What is the best time of year to visit Korea? Spring brings cherry blossoms in April, autumn brings foliage in October and November, and winter is the season for hot springs and quieter travel.
- Is tipping expected in Korea? No. Tipping is not customary anywhere in Korea, including restaurants, taxis, and hotels.
- How is IEUM different from a travel agent? A travel agent books what already exists. IEUM designs what does not, opening access through relationships built over years in Korea.
- How far in advance should I book? Four to six weeks gives the best access to reservations and experiences that fill early, though shorter timelines are regularly accommodated.
